checks.s: The deliverable contains a section titled or addressing Deviation/CAPA Ownership & Timelines that references §7.3.
The deliverable contains a section titled or addressing Right to Audit / For-Cause Triggers that references §9.1–9.2.
The deliverable contains a section titled or addressing Change Control Authority that references §8.1.
The deliverable contains a section titled or addressing APQR Responsibility that references §10.4.
The deliverable contains a section addressing Release/Rejection Authority & Regulatory Notification.
That section references both §6.2 and §12.1.
For §7.3, the deliverable presents Vantara's ideal position, at least one intermediate fallback or concession, and the floor/walk-away position.
For §9.1–9.2, the deliverable presents Vantara's ideal position, at least one intermediate fallback or concession, and the floor/walk-away position.
For §8.1, the deliverable presents Vantara's ideal position, at least one intermediate fallback or concession, and the floor/walk-away position.
For §10.4, the deliverable presents Vantara's ideal position, at least one intermediate fallback or concession, and the floor/walk-away position.
For §6.2/§12.1, the deliverable presents Vantara's ideal position, at least one intermediate fallback or concession, and the floor/walk-away position.

The §7.3 compromise proposes classification mechanisms and timelines between Vantara's position (Vantara classifies all deviations within 24 hrs; CAPA closure within 30 calendar days) and Prismara's position (Prismara classifies; notifies Vantara of Critical deviations within 48 hrs; CAPA closure within 90 days).
The §7.3 compromise uses tiered deviation classification with different notification timelines based on severity, distinguishing at least Critical deviations from other severities.
The §9.1–9.2 compromise separately addresses routine audit frequency and for-cause audit triggers or notice periods as distinct sub-provisions.
The audit compromise proposes routine audit frequency of 2 to 4 per year.
The audit compromise sets for-cause triggers broader than 'confirmed OOS only' but does not grant unlimited for-cause audit rights.
The audit rights discussion references Prismara's 7 concurrent MAH clients at the Durham facility as relevant context.
The audit rights discussion references the two Form 483 observations from the April 2025 FDA inspection (cleaning validation, environmental monitoring trending) as relevant context.
The §8.1 compromise distinguishes at least critical, major, and minor change categories and specifies different approval or notification requirements for each tier.
The §8.1 compromise falls between Vantara's position (prior written approval for all changes) and Prismara's position (approval for critical only; notification for major; minor at CMO discretion).
The §10.4 compromise proposes an authorship model that resolves the dispute between Vantara authoring and Prismara authoring for its site.
The §10.4 compromise specifies a data delivery timeline.
The deliverable acknowledges that Prismara identified APQR site authorship as a hard limit per the position letter.
The §10.4 compromise addresses or works around Prismara's hard limit on site authorship.
The §6.2 compromise addresses batch release and rejection authority by proposing a structure between Vantara's sole release authority and Prismara's site QA releasing to Vantara.

The §12.1 compromise addresses regulatory communication control by proposing a structure between Vantara controlling all FDA communications and Prismara independently responding to FDA 483s for its facility.
The compromise preserves Vantara's MAH obligations for product quality.
The compromise acknowledges Prismara's right or obligation to respond to inspectional findings at its own facility.
The deliverable includes proposed compromise clause language for §7.3 Deviation/CAPA in a form ready for insertion into the contract.
The deliverable includes proposed compromise clause language for §9.1–9.2 Audit Rights in a form ready for insertion into the contract.
The deliverable includes proposed compromise clause language for §8.1 Change Control in a form ready for insertion into the contract.
The deliverable includes proposed compromise clause language for §10.4 APQR in a form ready for insertion into the contract.
The deliverable includes proposed compromise clause language for §6.2 and §12.1 Release/Rejection & Regulatory Notification in a form ready for insertion into the contract.
The rationale references FDA 21 CFR Parts 210/211 or CGMP requirements.
The rationale explains how the compromise satisfies MAH responsibilities.
The rationale references ICH Q7 Section 16 (contract manufacturers and laboratories) in support of the proposed compromises.
The rationale references ICH Q10 Section 2.7 (management of outsourced activities) in support of the proposed compromises.
The rationale references EU GMP Annex 16 in the context of the release/rejection clause or dual-jurisdiction compliance.
The rationale acknowledges that Vantara holds BLA #761298 (FDA) and EU MA-EU-2025-0087431 (EMA), requiring dual-jurisdiction compliance.
The deliverable identifies at least one specific cross-clause trade-off, such as conceding on APQR authorship in exchange for stronger audit rights.
The §7.3 compromise requires Prismara to notify Vantara of Critical deviations within a timeframe strictly less than 48 hours.
The §7.3 compromise does not require Vantara to classify all deviations within 24 hours as Vantara's position unchanged.

The §7.3 compromise specifies different notification windows for Critical, Major, and Minor deviations, or otherwise specifies at least three distinct deviation treatment categories with different notification windows.
The §7.3 compromise proposes a CAPA closure timeline of 30 to 90 calendar days, inclusive.
The §7.3 compromise provides for documented CAPA closure extensions when root cause complexity justifies additional time and requires Vantara's approval for any extension.
The §9.1–9.2 compromise enumerates specific for-cause audit triggers beyond confirmed OOS, such as confirmed deviations, recalls, regulatory actions, or patient safety concerns.
The §9.1–9.2 compromise does not grant Vantara unlimited for-cause audit rights.
The §6.2 compromise establishes a two-step release process that preserves Prismara's site-level QA review or disposition role and Vantara's ultimate/final release and rejection authority.

The release clause discussion separately addresses EU QP certification by Dr. Yvonne Kleiber under Annex 16 for product destined for the EU market and references EU Marketing Authorization MA-EU-2025-0087431.
The §12.1 compromise acknowledges Prismara's right and obligation to respond to FDA Form 483 observations directed at its own facility.
The §12.1 compromise gives Vantara advance copies of any 483 response concerning the Velicitab™ product or shared processes/equipment and the right to review and comment before submission.
The regulatory communication discussion acknowledges that Prismara's 483 observation on cleaning validation relates to shared equipment.

The deliverable cites industry benchmarking data from 18 comparable sterile injectable CMO quality agreements and references benchmark positions, such as deviation notification, CAPA closure, or audit frequency ranges, to support the proposed compromises.
The deliverable acknowledges the December 31, 2025 execution deadline for the Quality Agreement.
The deliverable cites $23.1M lost revenue for Vantara and a $4.6M idle-capacity penalty for Prismara under MSA §14.2.
The deliverable uses those financial consequences as part of the strategic rationale for both parties to accept compromise.
The deliverable identifies Prismara's hard limit on independent 483 response authority from the position letter.
The deliverable explains how the compromise addresses or works around Prismara's hard limit on independent 483 response authority.
The deliverable identifies Prismara's hard limit on authoring the APQR for its site operations from the position letter.
The deliverable explains how the compromise addresses or works around Prismara's hard limit on APQR site authorship.

The deliverable presents the proposed compromise language as consistent with the FDA's September 2016 Guidance on quality agreements for contract manufacturing, including the principle that the MAH cannot delegate away its ultimate CGMP responsibilities.
The §8.1 compromise requires Vantara's prior written approval for at least critical changes.
The §8.1 compromise requires at least periodic notification or summary reporting to Vantara for minor changes and does not give Prismara full discretion over them without reporting.
The deliverable identifies that the Responsibility Matrix (Exhibit B) must be updated to align with the compromise positions adopted for the five contested clauses.
The deliverable notes the 'TBD — Under Negotiation' cells that must be completed.
The §9.1–9.2 compromise sets routine audit notice at least fifteen (15) business days and strictly less than thirty (30) calendar days.
The §9.1–9.2 compromise proposes a routine audit frequency of 2 to 4 per year, inclusive.
The deliverable uses document reference number QA-VAN-PRM-2025-001 when referencing the Quality Agreement.

The deliverable uses the Draft 3 section references correctly: §6.2 (Release/Rejection), §7.3 (Deviation/CAPA), §8.1 (Change Control), §9.1–9.2 (Audit), §10.4 (APQR), and §12.1 (Regulatory Notification).
The deliverable addresses dual-jurisdiction requirements under FDA and EMA throughout, referencing Vantara's BLA #761298 and EU MA-EU-2025-0087431.
The compromise language avoids compliance gaps under either jurisdiction.
The §7.3 compromise assigns initial deviation classification to Prismara as the site with first-hand knowledge and preserves Vantara's right to reclassify deviations upward in severity after review.
